label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON'S VICTORY.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEARING ALLIED HEADQUARTERS.

label: paragraph_title
text: BLOW STRUCK AT HEART OF NORTHERNERS' TERRITORY.

label: text
text: Following up their surprise advantage, the southerners are now striking at the very heart of Sun Chuan-fang's territory. Hostilities on three of the four sectors in the Kiangsi front are of little consequence at the moment.

label: text
text: Both sides are concentrating on one part of the front in a desperate struggle and the Cantonese are winning again.

label: text
text:
[By Our Special Correspondent.]
General Li Chung-yen (of Kwangsi), who commands the 7th Nationalist Army, is the Cantonese hero of the hour.

label: text
text: Before embarking on the northern expedition, this 7th Army had little experience of warfare. Whether it is due to the inspiration of victory, or to Russian strategy, these hitherto untrained troops have brought off the coup of the present war.

label: text
text: Along the Yangtse, the allies had one column marching on. Wuchang until held up at Hwangchow. An armistice has been declared on this sector, it is reported.

label: text
text:
Squeezed in Between.
The centre column was making overland for Changsha and Yo-chow to cut the Cantonese line of communication. This is now in hilly country near Shaoshui.
The southern column, after retaking Nanchang from the Nationalists had marched out to Kao-an and fought two battles.
In between the northern and centre sectors, General Li Chungen stole up to an advanced position, met difficulty in extricating himself, and then surprised Te-an.

label: text
text:
Northerners Withdrawn.
He has only about 5,000 troops with him. Unless there is an allied debacle, there is no immediate prospect of other southern de-tachments joining hands with him.

label: text
text: Nevertheless, General Li has deflected northwards, leaving Nanchang to colleagues further south, and is making for Kiukiang where he hopes to catch Sun Chuan-fang's headquarters unawares.

label: text
text: Several engagements have been fought by this mobile division of the 7th army and the northern allies are falling back.

label: text
text: To stem the advance of General Li, Sun Chuan-fang is bringing back his men posted along the Yangtse.

label: text
text:
On Way to Success.
Shoud Kiukiang fall, the Canonese will then have accomplished the first big step towards sub-
uing the “allied 5 provinces.”

label: text
text: Sun Chuan-fang still has the territorial advantage. His centre and southern columns can both wheel round and attack Gen. Li from the rear. But as they are also facing. an enemy on their front they show no immediate desire to take this step.

label: text
text: "The allies seem to be relying on the troops being withdrawn from advanced positions along the Yangtse who—it is expected—will return down river, land, and make a stand at or near Kiukiang."

label: paragraph_title
text: Throwing in Reserves.

label: text
text: That the situation is dangerous is evident from Sun Chuanfang's throwing in several brigades of fresh reserves.

label: text
text:
Several thousand strong, these are going to the railway and taking up posts along which Gen. Li is making for.
Unless a general armistice supervenes, it will be fight to a finish along the Kiukiang-Nanchang Railway with the odds at present slightly in favour of the more enterprising southerners.

label: text
text: Sun Chuan-fang's claim to the capture of Wuchang-hsien is not borne out.

label: text
text: The following is published by courtesy of the Naval authorities in Hong Kong:—

label: text
text: Fighting is reported in the immediate vicinity of Kiukiang, to defend which Marshal Sun Chuan-fang has recalled 7,000 troops from Wusueh.

label: text
text:
H.M.S. "Gnat has proceeded to Klukiang.
(Note: Klukiang is in the north of Kiangsi, the northern terminal of the Kiu-kiang-Nan-chang Railway. Te-an is in the middle of the line. Sun Chuan-fang's base is at Klukiang, whence his men have gone (west

label: text
text: wards) up the Yangtse towards Wuchang, but are now with-drawing to defend the home camp).

label: paragraph_title
text: At Wuchang.

label: text
text: The siege of Wuchang continues unabated.

label: text
text: Yesterday and today more non-combatants were allowed to leave the city, including several foreigners, while it is understood that similar facilities are being extended for the next several days.—Reuter.

label: text
text: March to Nanchang. " Han Plow Oct

label: text
text: It is reported that the southerners have commenced a fresh and more powerful drive to Nanchang, under the personal direction of General Chang Kai-shek.

label: text
text: Despite assurances to the contrary, steamers are again being subjected to rifle fire, this time in the vicinity of Hwangchow.

label: text
text: Two Japanese steamers arrived yesterday, and Messrs'. Butterfield and Swire's "Shengking" to-day, badly riddled, though, fortunately, there were no casualties.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Wuchang Frenzy.

label: text
text: Yesterday numbers of civilians, reported to total about 2,000, were allowed to leave Wuchang by mutual consent of the contending parties.

label: text
text: There was a frenziéld stampede to the gate, which was opened for a short time only, with the result that numbers of women and children were thrown down and trampled to death.

label: text
text: The refugees were in a most pitiful condition, and, when interviewed, stated that conditions were appalling. Numbers of people had already died of starvation, while a similar fate awaits many others unless the blockade is speedily lifted.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: CAR AS SECURITY

label: paragraph_title
text: FOR JUDGMENT AGAINST OWNER.

label: text
text: CONDITION ON RETURN.

label: text
text: A car held in security for an amount in respect of which judgment had been given against the owner was the subject of a claim in the Summary Court this morning.

label: text
text: Kartar Singh, the owner of the car, claimed against Noor Ahmad for the return of the car in serviceable condition, or alternatively, $1,000 in default of this.

label: text
text: It was stated in the course of the case that the car had been handed over as security for payment of $473 in respect of which judgment on a promissory note with interest had been given against the present plaintiff.

label: text
text: Mr. L. D. Turner, for the plaintiff, said that he understood that there was an agreement between the parties that the car should be used by the defendant in certain ways and not in others and handed back in the condition in which it was received.

label: text
text: His Honour (Mr. Justice Wood) said that this must be an implied agreement as he had the actual undertaking before him.

label: text
text: said that his client had taken up the position all along that the plaintiff could have the car immediately the amount of the previous judgment was paid.

label: text
text: Mr. Turner indicated that his client was willing to pay the amount of this judgment into court and it was eventually agreed that this should be done and that the car be handed over to plaintiff to be examined by an expert mechanic as to its condition.

label: text
text:
His Honour indicated that in the event of damage being proved such an amount would be deducted from the sum paid in.
Leaves was then given for plaintiff to amend the writ to a claim for damages and the case was adjourned.

label: paragraph_title
text: TROUBLE OVER.

label: paragraph_title
text: An Understanding With

label: paragraph_title
text: Yang Sen.

label: text
text: NO MILITARY INTERFERENCE.

label: text
text: British Ships Not to be Boarded

label: text
text: After the unconditional return to the British authorities of the two steamers which had been held on the Yangtse River by General Yang Sen—a preliminary measure insisted upon as the condition precedent to further pourparlers—British Consular officers and General Yang Sen have discussed other matters relating to conditions on the Yangtse.

label: text
text: The situation as affecting British interests there, partly as a result of these conversations, shows district improvement and there is likely to be a discontinuance in future of military interference with British merchant shipping within an extensive area under General Yang Sen's jurisdiction.

label: paragraph_title
text: Soldiers Must Pay.

label: text
text: In future the habit of Chinese troops to travel on river steamers without payment will have to be discontinued. Henceforth no such troops will be allowed to board British vessels.

label: text
text: Chungking, on the upper Yangtse, is reported to be quiet.

label: text
text: Vessels of the British Naval flotilla are proceeding up river to normal winter stations — British Wireless Service.

text: The following is published by courtesy of the Naval authorities in Hong Kong:—

label: text
text: H.M.S. "Widgeon" leaves at day-light to-morrow (Thursday) for Chungking.

label: text
text:
While removing earth from the site of a landslide, a coolle was killed by a boulder slipping from a new landslide a little further up the incline.
This occurred yesterday near the new road above, Conduit Road,
A ½-ton boulder crashed on to the man, injuring his left side. A rib was fractured and there were internal injuries, the man dying half an hour after admittance into hospital.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: PICKETS STILL AT SAMCHUN

label: text
text: Dictator Said to be Keen on "Settlement."

label: text
text: ل

label: text
text: General Chang Kai-shek, the virtual dictator of the Canton Government, is reported to have cabled back that he may return before October 10 if his presence is imperative.

label: text
text: Rumour says that the present leaders in Canton have cabled the commander-in-chief who is preoccupied with a momentous struggle in Kiangsi. But if the settlement can only be achieved by his being on the spot he may return.

label: text
text: There is no change to report except that an improved tone continues, following the Canton Government's statement that communications will be restored after October 10.

label: text
text: Strike pickets are still on duty at Samchun (across the New Territory border), examining the usual quota of from 100 to 200 passengers who travel daily on the railway between Canton and Kowloon.

label: text
text: No indication has been noticed of a general withdrawal of pickets to Canton from outports for the promised demobilisation.

label: text
text:
A message from Canton states that Mr. Eugene Chen, the Foreign Minister of the Canton Nationalist Government has informed the (British?) Consul at Shameen that his Government has now definitely decided to resume communication between Canton and Hongkong in pursuance of the intention to terminate the boycott.—British Wireless Service.
A combined meeting has been held between representatives of all classes and the Strike Committee.

label: text
text: It was resolved that after communications between "Canton and Hong Kong" had been restored, an organisation be formed to promote the development of Chinese products.

label: text
text: Another decision arrived at was that the Strike movement would be withdrawn but that other bodies would be formed to assist trade and protect labour—"Wah Tsz Yat Po."

label: paragraph_title
text: PRESENT POLICY.

label: text
text:
Rumours As To War Memoria
Scheme

label: text
text: A question on which it is possible that there may be discussion at the Budget debate to take place shortly is that concerning the future of the Government Civil Hospital.

label: text
text: Some considerable time ago it was generally understood that the present site of the Hospital was recognised to be unsatisfactory in that it is difficult of access and in a congested, noisy area.

label: text
text: At that time it was understood that the Hospital was to be pulled down and rebuilt at Morrison Hill but this is not contemplated in the present policy of the Government. The “China Mail” understands that, although no work has yet been put in hand and no vote passed, it is the present intention of the Government to rebuild the Hospital entirely on a site adjacent to the present Hospital (the area at present devoted to tennis lawn, etc.) and it is also gathered that the scheme provides for the present site of the Hospital being converted into public gardens.

label: text
text:
That the Hospital is in a quarter of the city entirely Chinese is not regarded as a drawback, having regard to the fact that it is mainly concerned with service to the Chinese residents.
The scheme for rebuilding will naturally be a costly one and it is stated that, if and when carried through, it will amount to something like three million dollars.

label: paragraph_title
text: Peak Hospital Future

label: text
text: It is also rumoured that there may be a change in policy with regard to the War Memorial Nursing Home, a scheme having been brought forward, it is stated, whereby the Peak Hospital might be enlarged, and considerably improved, the scheme being incorporated in that which originally had, as its object the separate erection above the Peak Road of a War Memorial Nursing Home.

label: text
text: If this, in fact, meets with the approval of those who are concerned, then work on the War Memorial Nursing Home would not proceed and efforts would be concentrated on the Peak Hospital improvements.

label: text
text: Upon enquiry in official circles, the “China Mail” was informed that a formula was being sought which would meet with the approval of those concerned. No decision had yet been reached.

label: text
text: in this connection, it may be recalled that for some time the Government has run the Peak Hospital which was lent to it rent free as the result of the action of a public spirited gentleman.

label: text
text: In addition to ascertaining his views, there is, of course, the question of consulting the trustees representing subscribers, both Chinese and foreign, to the War Memorial scheme the Government interest by reason of its contribution and the legal questions involved in any possible change of policy.
